item.title: Hurricanes 5, Islanders 3
item.description: ELMONT, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 05: Brandon Bussi #32 of the Carolina Hurricanes saves a shot from Anthony Duclair #11 of the New York Islanders during the first period at UBS Arena on November 05, 2026 in Elmont, New York. (Photo by Steven Ryan/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images According to coach Rod Brind’Amour the team was “not at its best”, but the Carolina Hurricanes scored twice in the third period and held on to defeat the New York Islanders, 5-3 on Thursday night at UBS Arena. The Canes improved their record to 13-3-2 on the season. Brandon Bussi made 24 saves on the 27 shots he faced to pick up his third win of the season. Logan Stankoven got things started just 57 seconds into the game when he took a pass from Jackson Blake and ripped it past goalie Semyon Varlamov. Stankoven now has a team leading 11 goals for the season. Blake added to his team-high assist total to 14. A couple of minutes later, Jesperi Kotkaniemi tipped in a Jordan Martinook pass to make it 2-0 and it looked like Carolina was flying. But they took their feet off the gas and the Islanders got back in the game. The home team tied the score at two but the Canes would strike again on an Andrei Svechnokov goal in the second. The Islanders tied it at three before the end of the period and even though the Canes were outshooting NY, they seemed to be reeling a bit. But they came out strong in the third period. Will Carrier knocked in the game-winner off a Svechnikov shot 15 minutes and change into the third and that would be enough to finish off the Islanders. Jalen Chatfield fought for a loose puck and put in a long shot into an empty net to complete the scoring. All in all, it was the team’s best effort but they did what they needed to do to get the win. Next up will be a game at home on Saturday night against the Blackhawks which will be their last game before the trip to Finland. Notes: Kotkaniemi had a team low 8 minutes of ice time. He now has 5 goals and 3 assists and has played well recently. Not sure what else he needs to do to see more ice time. He also had 2 hits and was 50% in the faceoff circle. Taylor Hall returned to action and played just over 10 minutes. The Canes went 34% in the circle. The Hurricanes ended up outshooting the home team, 39-27. item.title: Jaguars move up in AFC standings after squashing Ravens
item.description: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars won on Thursday night and moved up in the AFC standings. With the Pittsburgh Steelers on a bye, the Jags’ position will be at least third by the end of the weekend, and they can move into second and a tie for first place if everything goes their way. Let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves. Here are the standings as we stand now, then we will get into the rest of the weekend. AFC playoff standings after the Jaguars win 1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) 2. Denver Broncos (6-2, 3-1 AFC) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, 5-2) 4. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, 3-2 AFC) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (5-2, 5-1 AFC) 6. Cincinnati Bengals (5-2, 4-2 AFC) 7. New England Patriots (5-3, 5-1 AFC) 8. Cleveland Browns (5-3, 3-3 AFC) 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5) 11. Houston Texans (2-5) 12. New York Jets (2-6, 2-3 AFC) 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-6, 1-5 AFC) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-6) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) Explaining the 6-2 tiebreaker between the Jaguars, Steelers, and Broncos The Jaguars, Broncos, and Steelers all go in together and while they will all play each other eventually, that hasn’t happened so we skip the head-to-head-to-head tiebreaker. The tiebreaker moves to conference record where the 3-1 Broncos best the 5-2 Jaguars and the 3-2 Steelers. Denver is the two seed. The Broncos and Steelers haven’t played each other yet, so the AFC record is applied again here and the 5-2 Jaguars slip ahead of the 3-2 Steelers. Jacksonville is the three seed and Pittsburgh is the four seed. How high in the standings can the Jaguars get before the end of Week 8? The Steelers are on a bye, but the Jaguars are already ahead of them. The Broncos can lose to the Carolina Panthers and fall to 6-3. The Buffalo Bills, though, can’t fall behind Jacksonville. The Bills could lose to the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night to fall into that 6-2 tie, but they are 5-1 in the AFC and that isn’t going to change. The highest the Jaguars can get is second behind Buffalo — for now.

item.title: UNC vs. Wofford game preview, info, prediction and more
item.description: The North Carolina Tar Heels return to action on Friday night, looking to go 2-0 on the young college basketball season. But in order to do that, they are going to need to play better than they did in their season-opening win over Western Carolina. While UNC got a win, they had to hold off a Catamounts team that pushed them to the end. UNC played poorly on both sides of the court and, honestly, are a little lucky they were able to win the game. But a win is a win and North Carolina is moving forward and focusing on the second game in the Michael Malone era. Next up? The Wofford Terriers. The Tar Heels' schedule gets tougher moving forward, so racking up some wins here early on will be key. It could also help them earn some more confidence as well before that schedule picks up. While there were struggles in the first game, this is another opportunity. It's one in which they can use to figure some things out in terms of rotations and defensive sets. This will give Malone a chance to see some things with his roster on the court as well. Key to Victory Rebounding. The Tar Heels were outrebounded by the Catamounts 41-32 on Monday night and it almost cost them the game. It's unusual to see this program get outrebounded by an inferior opponent, even with it being the season-opener. North Carolina's roster doesn't have a dominant big man just yet and they are going to rely on Sayon Keita to be that guy. With Cameron Fenns ineligible, the depth takes a hit. The Tar Heels cant afford to keep being bad at rebounding because it's going to cost them if they do. Something to Watch Point guard role. In the season opener, we saw Neo Avdalas be the primary ball-handler on offense. But it didn't work out so well. The lack of a true point guard really hurt them in the opener. Will Malone make an adjustment? And if so, then who? This team may not have a true point guard option ready to go at the moment which could hurt them. item.description: The 49ers pulled off a blockbuster trade ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. item.title: Fort Defiance volleyball cruises to regional final
item.description: After more than a week off, Fort Defiance showed no signs of rust in its playoff opener Nov. 5. The top seed in Region 2B rolled over No. 4 Clarke County 25-11, 25-10, 25-20 in the Region 2B semifinals. With the win, Fort Defiance will host No. 2 Madison County for the regional championship Nov. 10. Both teams have already earned a spot in the Class 2 state playoffs. Fort Defiance was on fire from the start. They didn't have a single serving or hitting error in the opening set, setting the tone for the night. The 75-minute match was short work for Fort, which is aiming to reach the state championship game for the third season in a row. Junior Caroline Hanger couldn't remember playing a set with no errors. "It was just great. Everything was just flowing," said Hanger, who finished with 10 kills. "All the hitters were doing so good and the defense was picking everything up." Freshman Maddie Gale had another all-around good game, finishing with six kills, 18 assists and four aces. Senior libero Norah Anderson had nine digs and four aces, while junior middle Harper Carter had six kills and sophomore Abbi Bright had seven digs and Alexis Miller added six assists in the win. "I think if we keep playing like how we played tonight, I feel confidence in our skills," said Hanger. Coach Amber Pitsenbarger did a lot of skill work with her players throughout the week without any games because of a first-round playoff bye, but maybe the biggest factor in keeping Fort sharp was how the coaching staff approached last Thursday and this past Tuesday, which would have typically been game days. "We went through the game-day routine," Pitsenbarger said. "We did our serve-around routine and we actually just played." The coach said they had a match between starters and non-starters and some other scrimmages just to stay sharp. It helped. Hanger liked having the week off, saying the team probably needed it after a long regular season, but she liked staying in the game-day routine even without an actual game that counted. Next up is Madison, which advanced to play Fort with a four-set win over No. 6 Stuarts Draft. Madison won 25-19, 25-17, 16-25, 25-19. Addyson Dameron had 25 assists and nine digs to lead Draft, while Lily May added 16 kills and Kylie Morland had 15 kills and 10 digs in the loss. Addy Coyner and Serenity Hamric both finished with 10 digs. Madison enters the match unbeaten at 23-0, but they did lose to Fort Defiance in a scrimmage in mid-August. "We played them in a scrimmage but it was very, very early," Pitsenbarger said. "We know they're going to be good. We've ended their season several times so we know they're going to be coming for us. I expect it to be a really good matchup." item.title: Kozo Tashima: Japan leader looking to bring 'integrity' to FIFA
item.description: Kozo Tashima has announced he intends to run for the FIFA presidency (Toshifumi KITAMURA) Kozo Tashima first started playing football after watching the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, and since then he has dedicated his life to developing the sport's growth in Japan. The 68-year-old is set to become the first person from Japan to run for the FIFA presidency after announcing he would stand against Gianni Infantino in football's governing body's election in March. Tashima has served as a football player, coach and bureaucrat and has a reputation for being a safe pair of hands. He rarely makes headlines, and one of the few times he appeared outside the sport pages was when he became one of the first public figures in Japan to contract coronavirus in March 2020. He spent time studying at the German Sport University Cologne and said the experience changed the way he saw sport's purpose in society. He says his decision to run for the FIFA presidency was based on a belief that "in this age of business and money, sport must firmly uphold its integrity". "The worst thing would be if he (Infantino) were to continue without an election," he told reporters after announcing his candidacy. "I feel this is a test of whether FIFA has the ability to cleanse itself." Tashima was born in southern Kumamoto and captained his team to the title in Japan's prestigious national high school championship. With no professional football in the country at the time, he had ambitions of becoming a PE teacher and enrolled at a university, where he was called up to play for Japan's full national team. He joined a club in Japan's amateur league after graduating but soon retired as a player and went to Germany to study to become a coach. He described his "profound shock" at the players' superior skills and the way football was viewed there. "Even back in 1980, the training in Germany was hugely scientific and systematic," he said. "Everything seemed like a different world from Japan, and it was a big culture shock for me." - Experienced hand - Tashima returned home determined to use what he had learned in Germany and help develop Japanese football. He coached a university team before joining the Japan Football Association (JFA), where he worked on development programmes and coached the country's national teams at various youth levels. He rose through the JFA ranks and was elected president in 2016, while also serving on the Asian Football Confederation executive committee and the FIFA Council. His reign as JFA chief saw him fire Japan coach Vahid Halilhodzic two months before the 2018 World Cup in Russia. Halilhodzic, who was unpopular with the players, was replaced by Akira Nishino, and Japan reached the last 16, where they were eliminated by Belgium. "Some people told me that I wasn't the one who hired Halilhodzic so it wouldn't be my fault if the team lost," Tashima said. "But as president, all the responsibility lay with me." The decision left plenty of fans and analysts convinced that the SEC is getting the benefit of the doubt from the committee once again. Now, Danny Kanell is predicting things are going to get even worse. The former Florida State quarterback warned that there will be a push for an 8-4 SEC team to make the playoff this season. Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Alabama has losses to Georgia and Tennessee this season, including a 26-10 defeat in Knoxville on Oct. 17. Even so, the committee ranked the Crimson Tide at No. 5, making them one of the highest-ranked two-loss teams in College Football Playoff history. To make matters worse for critics, Tennessee came in all the way down at No. 13, outside of the playoff field. Texas, which beat Tennessee in that same stadium back in September, was ranked two spots behind Alabama at No. 7. The debate also comes as the playoff is set to grow even bigger. Last month, the CFP was reportedly nearing a deal to expand to 24 teams beginning in 2027, which Kanell supported. “I think this could be a great day for college football. I’m actually excited,” Kanell said at the time, on CBS Sports . ‘Brace Yourselves’ Needless to say, the decision to rank Alabama all the way at No. 5 received a lot of pushback. While a lot of the criticism was directed at Alabama specifically, Kanell took aim at the SEC as a whole, predicting an even bigger push for the conference this postseason. “I hope everyone is prepared for the push for an 8-4 SEC team in the college football playoff. THIS year. Brace yourselves. It’s coming. They have no shame,” Kanell wrote on X . Not everyone agreed with Kanell’s logic, though. Several pointed out that his support for a 24-team playoff would open the door for teams with even more losses. “As opposed to your 24-team CFP where they’ll push for a 7-5 SEC team – great work!” wrote Josh Pate , college football analyst for ESPN, On3, and Yahoo Sports. “you meant 5-7…7 good SEC losses – huge resume builders,” Kanell replied . “But with the 24 team CFP that’s gonna be pretty much automatic. Choose your fighter brother,” wrote Jake Crain , host of On3’s Crain & Cone . Former Georgia star David Pollack, host of See Ball Get Ball , decided to have some fun with it. “It Just Means More! Going to be sweet @CFBPlayoff #bestconference #toptobottom,” Pollack wrote . The controversy isn’t going to stop anytime soon. But maybe next year, the 24-team playoff could help the debate a little bit with more teams included in the field. item.title: ‘Not even close’- Draymond Green fires back at Kendrick Perkins after brutal ‘liability’ claim
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Draymond Green has fired back at Kendrick Perkins after the ESPN analyst labelled the Golden State Warriors forward a liability rather than an asset following his latest ejection. Green acknowledged that he is no longer the player he once was, but insisted his basketball intelligence still separates him from his former NBA rival. The exchange followed Golden State’s 116-113 victory over the Phoenix Suns, during which Green was ejected after a heated altercation involving Suns centre Khaman Maluach and Dillon Brooks. Draymond Green questions Kendrick Perkins’ basketball intelligence Perkins had criticised Green during an appearance on ESPN’s First Take, questioning whether his focus had shifted away from basketball and towards on-court confrontations. He also pointed to Green’s lack of production early in the season, suggesting the Warriors were not getting enough from the four-time All-Star. Perkins said: “Listen, when was the last time we discussed Draymond Green and brought him up for his basketball and not fighting? At some point, he has to deliver on the floor. When you look at the start of this season, Draymond Green has been non-existent.” He added: “He has done absolutely nothing for the Golden State Warriors. To me, he has been a liability more than an asset.” Green responded on his podcast, The Draymond Green Show, admitting that his physical abilities have declined while taking aim at Perkins’ own playing career. The Warriors star said: “Kendrick Perkins said Draymond Green is a liability, he ain’t no asset no more. And guess what Kendrick Perkins … at 36-years-old, to be 37 this year, I am 1000 percent not the player I once was … I’m not even close to the player I once was.” He continued: “But, Kendrick Perkins, the difference between myself and big dummies like you is I can think. And so when your body didn’t move the same no more, you weren’t as athletic as you once were, it looked a little different for you cause you weren’t the smartest basketball player.” Green’s early-season numbers give Perkins’ criticism some context. Across six appearances, he is averaging 3.2 points, 5.0 rebounds and 6.3 assists per game, while shooting 38.9 per cent from the field. His latest ejection came after he forcefully brought Maluach to the floor, prompting Brooks to step in and confront him. Green later defended the play, arguing that a centre must stand up for himself to maintain respect around the basket. The Warriors have won five consecutive games after opening the season with three defeats, and Green will now be under pressure to turn his response into more consistent performances on the court. item.title: Blackhawks Lose 4-1 To Lightning, Now Dropped Five Straight Games
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (4-12-1) lost for the second time in as many nights and for the fifth game in a row on Thursday, falling 4-1 to the Tampa Bay Lightning (10-3-2) at Benchmark International Arena. The Blackhawks remain winless on the road this season, dropping to 0-7-1 in eight games. The Lightning remain undefeated at home, moving to 8-0-0. Former Blackhawks forward Ilya Mikheyev scored twice, including the game-winning goal, in his first game against his old team since signing with Tampa Bay in free agency this past summer. Victor Hedman (PP) and Ryan McDonagh also scored for the Lightning. McDonagh had a plus-three rating, while his defensive partner, Erik Cernak, added two assists with a plus-three rating. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 26 shots and has now won 15 of 16 career regular-season games against the Blackhawks. He’s allowed just 33 goals in those 16 games. Roman Kantserov was the only reason Vasilevskiy didn’t record his second career shutout against the Blackhawks, with the rookie snapping his fellow countryman’s shutout bid with 48.1 seconds left in the third period. It was Kantserov’s team-leading eighth goal of the season, which extended his current point streak to seven games. Sam Rinzel and Ethan Del Mastro tallied assists on the goal, marking back-to-back games with assists for both defensemen. Arvid Soderblom made his fourth start of the season and stopped 31 of 35 shots. Soderblom remains winless in 2026-27. For the second straight game, the Blackhawks fell behind 2-0 in the first period and never recovered. While they rallied for three goals in the final 40 minutes on Wednesday, there wasn’t much of an offensive pushback in the second and third periods against Tampa Bay. The Blackhawks registered only nine high-danger scoring chances in 60 minutes, as they struggled to find time and space with possession against the Lightning defense. They’ve now scored two goals or fewer in 11 of 17 games this season. Perhaps the only positive from Thursday’s loss was the Blackhawks increased physicality, leading 31-13 in hits. One night ago, the Hawks had only 12 hits and were pushed around in a 5-3 loss to the Florida Panthers. Scrappy fourth-liner Dillon Boucher led the team with seven hits in 8:12 of ice time, while also getting into a must-see scrap, his first NHL fight, against Jeff Viel in the second period. Boucher’s linemate, Cole Smith, was one of the better Blackhawks in Tampa and chipped in with six hits. That’s a significant step in the right direction for the Blackhawks in that aspect. Now, they just have to figure out how to score and keep the puck out of their own net… Here are highlights from the Blackhawks 4-1 loss in Tampa Bay. Anthony Cirelli found a soft spot between Frank Nazar and Alex Vlasic on the entry, then found Hedman streaking to the net for his fourth goal of the season.

item.description: Harbor Teacher sophomore Layla Phillips watches her tee shot soar down the fairway at the CIF City Section girls' golf championships at Balboa Golf Course in Encino on Thursday. (Steve Galluzzo / For The Times) When asked what part of her golf game has improved the most since last year, Layla Phillips cited mental toughness. The 15-year-old from Harbor Teacher Prep needed it to repeat as the City Section individual champion Thursday at Balboa Golf Course in Encino, shooting a one-under-par 71 to win by one stroke over fellow sophomore Lauren Song of Palisades, who led going to the 18th hole but four-putted for a double bogey. “I was nervous going to the last hole because I know Lauren’s a great player,” said Phillips, who carded a five-under-par 67 last fall to win by six strokes over Macy Lee of El Camino Real. “My first shot went left, hers was in the center of the fairway and after our second shots, she’s on the green and I’m not.” Phillips caught a bad break when her approach to the green hit a tree branch on its upward flight and dropped 20 yards short of the green. Read more: Prep talk: Three-sport standout Kai Beary plays role for 27-0 JSerra flag football team “I’d chipped that same shot a few times earlier in the round and didn’t put enough on it, so I took a risk and rolled it to within seven feet,” she said. “The par putt was uphill, breaking to the right and I was trying to trust myself, take deep breaths and give myself an image of where to hit it. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The lack of goal-scoring depth came back to the fore for the Detroit Red Wings on Thursday, and it bit them in a 2-1 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights. Last week, he joined greats Marshall Faulk and Marcus Allen in an exclusive rushing touchdown club. In doing so, he tied Faulk for seventh on the list of most touchdowns in NFL history. This week, it’s LaDainian Tomlinson’s turn to be overtaken by Henry. At age 32, Henry remains highly productive for the Ravens. Heading into Thursday night, he had already racked up 632 yards with eight touchdowns in eight games. item.title: Suburban gymnast to represent Team USA at World Championships
item.description: DOWNERS GROVE, Ill. ( WGN ) - A teenage gymnast from the southwest suburbs is set to represent Team USA at the World Championships next week in China, but before becoming one of the best in the world, he almost quit the sport. As one of the best trampoline gymnasts in the country, Freddie Wanat knows a bit about taking a leap. "Once I hit the mini and I like get up in the air, it just feels like I'm flying," he said. Before you can soar, sometimes you stumble and Wanat learned that early. He started gymnastics at nine years old and almost quit the sport by the time he turned 10. Loyola Academy running back shines for top-ranked Ramblers "It just felt like it was too much work. I just wanted to be more relaxed and like have more freedom," Wanat said. He told his coach "D'Robinson" that he'd rather be playing outside with his friends. "He's like, 'I don't want to be in the gym all day,' so when he said, 'I want to quit,' I'm like, 'You have so much more to give,'" D'Robinson said. Coach was indeed tough. Wanat received the blessing of raw talent, but Robinson said that wasn't enough and that he had to be willing to give something, too. "You've got to give it all you got. If it don't work, it don't work, but you've got to at least try," D'Robinson said. Building tied to Great Chicago Fire in danger of being demolished The message landed. Wanat is now a five-time U.S. Tumbling and Trampoline Association National Champion, who's name adorns on the wall at his gym, the Elite Sports Complex in Downers Grove. Wanat, a freshman in high school, is now "world bound" with Team USA. "It was very exciting to find out that I was going to Worlds," Wanat said. He'll be competing for his country next week in China and will be one of four Americans in his age group to compete in the difficult "double-mini" event. "The double mini is a long trampoline that kind of reminds people of the vault, and you do two or three skills on and I usually do two because it's the harder type of version," Wanat said. All the hours of training will come down to a single moment. Read more: Latest Chicago news and headlines "In this sport, you train 12 hours a week for only three seconds of your life," D'Robinson said. Wanat learned long ago, sometimes the most important moments don't involved the bright lights of a world competition. They're the quiet choices we make to believe in ourselves. "I realized I was like going to be really good at it, and I realized that I really shouldn't have quit, and I just kept going," Wanat said. Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. All rights reserved. item.description: Bruins' Upcoming Schedule Creates Major Opportunity After Penguins Win originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins have already established themselves as one of the NHL's more interesting teams during the opening weeks of the season, but their upcoming schedule could provide an even bigger opportunity. Boston defeated the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-2 on Thursday night, extending its winning streak to three games and improving to 12-4-1. The Bruins have now won 10 of their last 13 contests, putting together an impressive stretch against a variety of opponents. What comes next might be just as important as what Boston has already accomplished. The Bruins will play 10 of their next 11 games at TD Garden, giving them an extended opportunity to build momentum in front of their home crowd. Bruins Finally Put Road Struggles Behind Them Thursday's victory was significant for more than the six goals Boston scored against Pittsburgh. The Bruins entered the game having lost three consecutive road contests, creating a noticeable difference between their performances at home and away from TD Garden. Elias Lindholm doubles the Bruins' lead 🤩 Bruins 3 Penguins 1 https://t.co/ggDEkDyFMO — NESN (@NESN) November 6, 2026 Pavel Zacha scored twice against the Penguins, while Morgan Geekie, Elias Lindholm, Mark Kastelic and Fraser Minten also found the back of the net. Boston established control early and carried a three-goal advantage into the third period. Michael DiPietro made 16 saves, providing another dependable performance as the Bruins continued finding ways to win with contributions from throughout the roster. The victory also extended Boston's impressive recent record in Pittsburgh, where the Bruins have earned points in seven consecutive visits dating to November 2022. TD Garden Could Become A Major Advantage Boston begins a four-game homestand Sunday against the Florida Panthers, followed by games against Montreal, Minnesota and Los Angeles. The Bruins then make a brief trip to Detroit before returning home for another extended stretch. The schedule includes additional home games against Washington, Winnipeg, Toronto, Vancouver and Colorado before the beginning of December. That concentration of games at TD Garden creates an opportunity for the Bruins to establish consistency without the disruptions of repeated travel. It also gives the coaching staff more opportunities to manage preparation and recovery between contests. Boston has already demonstrated that it can perform well at home. The challenge now is maintaining that success against a variety of opponents, including several teams capable of testing the Bruins' defensive structure. But Orgeron left practice in mid-August after he wasn’t feeling well, and he went on to miss the rest of fall camp and LSU’s first few games. He’s doing better. He’s still not all the way back,” Kiffin said, via Jerit Roser . “He just means a lot to me. We’ve just been through a lot. And his passion. That’s how he is with everything. And sometimes that’s not always the best thing to follow,” Kiffin added. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox have quite a bit of work to do in the offseason. Most of the Red Sox issues had to do with a lack of hitting, particularly in the final month of the regular season and in the playoffs. Sonny Gray didn’t have great things to say about the Red Sox organization at the end of the season. WEEI Red Sox Insider Rob Bradford weighs in on whether he may be back with the team next year. @KenLairdWEEI @teddyjradio @heyrichhey pic.twitter.com/wnvVdjz7cD — Rich and Ken with Ted Johnson (@richkented) November 5, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) However, they may need to bring in starting pitching if they can’t re-sign ace pitcher Sonny Gray. After Garrett Crochet went down with an injury that kept him out from April until he was able to pitch in relief in the playoffs, Gray simply took over as the team’s best starting pitcher. He had an 18-5 record along with a 2.72 earned run average. Gray made 29 starts for the Red Sox and he pitched 169.0 innings. Unlike most of the top pitchers in the game, Gray is not a fireballer who depends on a 100-MPH fastball to blow hitters away. Instead, he is an old-school pitcher who induces weak contact and lets his fielders do the job. He regularly lives on the corners or forces hitters to swing at pitches out of the strike zone. Gray is a free agent and he will have the opportunity to get offers from teams that value his services. Red Sox insider Rob Bradford believes the Red Sox want Gray back, but it may be at their price . If Gray wants more, the Red Sox may be willing to let him move on. That would seem to be a foolish move. It appears that Gray, Payton Tolle and Ranger Suarez clearly fill important roles for the Red Sox starting staff and the belief is that Crochet will come back healthy next year. That would give the Red Sox four solid starters. However, if Gray leaves, they would need a new starter and perhaps one who can take over as an ace. Has Rohit Sharma played at Hnry Stadium? Wellington splits its international cricket between two grounds, and Rohit Sharma's record in the city is split between them. Hnry Stadium, previously known as Westpac and then Sky Stadium, takes the white-ball fixtures, while Tests are staged at the Basin Reserve a few minutes away. Rohit has batted twice at Hnry Stadium, once in an ODI in January 2014 and once in a T20I in February 2019. He was not in the side for India's other visit, the fourth T20I of the 2020 tour, and has played one Test at the Basin Reserve.
